head: 0d4faf7d4feda817499ea19e8797a0e03504fbad
review_scope: Current uncommitted trace.py mining timeout change and three new test_trace.py regressions; unchanged RPC.call, AnvilSession and guardian lifetime/cleanup inspected as dependencies.
conclusions: Only the owned local evm_mine call receives min(150, deadline-monotonic); it receives no fresh 150-second budget.
The transport timeout is restored in finally on success, RPC failure and any propagating BaseException; failure evaluating remaining budget occurs before assignment.
The change leaves read-only upstream and ordinary local method admission unchanged. Each replay owns its separate transport; no shared RPC object or global timeout is modified.

AnvilSession lifetime still derives from the same primitive deadline; its separate guardian expires or responds to owner pipe closure and owned context exit. This patch does not extend the guardian lifetime.
Follow-up block/receipt calls retain the normal read timeout, and remaining-budget checks still govern receipt iteration and candidate branch launch.

cases: slow mine gets 30-second remaining budget and restores 10-second reads
near deadline mine gets only 2.5 seconds
RPC failure restores timeout and exits owned context
focused_check.kind: Mocked transport/context regression; no Anvil, Docker, archive or model call

prior_observation_inspected.scope: Existing root-produced native observation; reviewer did not repeat the archive execution or independently re-probe the port.

limits: No actual slow archive-backed successful mining execution, real signal cancellation or real elapsed deadline probe was run by this reviewer; root-owned actual native execution and full suite remain separate evidence.

urllib socket timeout is an operation timeout, not itself whole-process cancellation. Existing node guardian and bounded-worker controls remain necessary; native Python owner whole-process safety is not claimed.
Node termination and context cleanup may require their existing cleanup grace periods; this review does not claim that every native caller returns at precisely 150 seconds.
The three tests use fixed monotonic time and validate timeout plumbing/context cleanup, not a real wall-clock mine duration.
Unchanged parent-state pool funding and full-block/opcode/end-state replay limits remain open.
Independent source review is not protected-main GitHub approval.
